top_problem: The grid is now exact: 36 pt ink margins on all four sides, item names at one x per column (49.5 and 325.5 pt), price right edges at one x per column (286.5 and 562.5 pt, 7 each), and every item, price, subhead and name band sits at one fixed offset on the 6 pt step from the deck top (item rows y mod 6 = 5.25 for 14/14, prices 4.5 for 14/14, subheads 1.5, name bands 0). But the card faces do not share that system. Verse text blocks start at 140.3, 194.5, 472.1 and 479.1 pt and are centred loosely. The La Botella figure is 45 pt against 105 to 111 pt on the other cards. Because of the 522 vs 456 pt card bottoms, only the top name bands line up across columns; the lower cards float. The boldest missing idea is to make each card a real portrait lotería card: a full-height figure panel, the name in a band across the foot, and the number chip in the corner, all four on one identical face template. The list would then run as the card's reverse, so the tabla reads as a deck rather than four boxed lists with landscape headers.
fixes: Put every card face on one template with the same face height (141 pt), figure box (105 x 105 pt at x = card + 36 pt) and verse column (one fixed left edge and width per column, e.g. card x + 150 pt). La Botella's 45 pt bottle and one-line verse currently break the system.

Make both column rows break on the same line (e.g. 450 / 12 / 156 on both sides, or match 384 / 318 by giving both top cards equal height) so the lower name bands and subheads line up across the 12 pt gutter as the top ones do.

Remove the printed 'glass / bottle TBC' placeholder under Brut Rosé (it also knocks one description element off the 0.75 pt baseline offset the other 13 share); print real glass and bottle columns or nothing.
Widen the 12 pt gutter to at least 18 pt (half the 36 pt margin) so the four heavy 3 pt frames stop crowding each other and the tabla reads as separate cards on a board.

Cut the accent set from five (terracotta, agave, agave blue, rosa, marigold) to four by folding agave blue into ink or agave, and give the one-line beer/wine/spirit descriptions a second line so the three thin cards carry the same density and rhythm as El Cantarito.

top_problem: Card headers and subheads are clean and aligned, but the masthead is the weakest part of the hierarchy. The top title is a generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' with no venue name. The 'IOWA CITY, IOWA' line overlaps the title box by 2.25 pt (title y 87 + h 29.25 = 116.25 pt against the location line at y 114 pt) and sits only 12.75 pt above the deck, off the 6 pt rhythm. Three of the four cards carry a single subhead that repeats the band gloss ('DRAFT & CIDER' under 'Beer & Cider', 'RED, WHITE & SPARKLING' over three wines). The boldest missing idea: the masthead should itself be a lotería card or tabla header (a named 'La Cantina' card with its own number and verse), so the title level belongs to the same system as the four cards instead of floating as plain type under the papel picado.

header_level_card_titles.x: centred as a name + gloss lockup in each band, so the Spanish name alone sits off the card centre (EL CANTARITO x 86.88, LA BOTELLA 101.87, EL BARRIL 372.75, LA ROSA 396.11)
header_level_card_titles.result: pass: one size, rows share one y

measurements.hierarchy_steps_pt: 12 card title / 10.5 item name / 7 subhead; the title-to-item step is only 1.5 pt, so the coloured band does all the work

masthead.result: fail: overlap, and spacing off the 6 pt grid

measurements.level_tagging: 'IOWA CITY, IOWA' is tagged subheader but is styled as a spaced grey locator, not as the bold DM Sans 700 caps section subhead: two styles at one level

fixes: Give the masthead a real venue name and put it on the deck's 6 pt rhythm: title bottom, location line and deck top on 6 pt steps (location to deck 18 pt, matching flags to title), with no overlap between the title and location boxes.

Remove the single subheads that repeat the band gloss (DRAFT & CIDER, AGAVE & BRANDY, RED, WHITE & SPARKLING) or make them add information (for example 'De barril · On draft', 'Por copa'), so subheads only appear where a card has two or more groups, as El Cantarito does.
Widen the gap between hierarchy levels: raise card titles to 14 pt, or take item names down to 10 pt, so the name band reads as a clear level above the items even in greyscale or phone view.

Centre the Spanish card name itself on the card axis and hang the English gloss off it (or set the gloss on a second line), so all four titles share one optical centre instead of shifting with the gloss length.
Re-tag or restyle 'IOWA CITY, IOWA' as its own 'locator' level, so the subheader level has one style across the document.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling
top_problem: The lotería palette works, but it has five chromatic colours (terracotta, agave green, agave blue, rosa, marigold) where the scorecard asks for 2-4 plus neutrals, and every numeral uses the same Fraunces 700 voice. So the loteria card numbers 44, 9, 41 and 8 read as prices sitting next to the real prices of 7-18, and a guest can take the '44' chip on the cocktail card for a price. The boldest idea still missing: the numerals are not a designed system. Card numbers should look like lotería card numbers (framed, in a different face or style) and prices should look like prices, each with its own clear role.
fixes: Set the loteria card numbers apart from prices: put them in Fraunces italic or an outlined or engraved numeral, or add a 'No.' prefix in the chip, so '44' can never be read as a $44 cocktail. Keep the prices as the only bold lining numerals.

Cut the palette to four chromatic colours: fold La Botella's agave blue #1E3F66 into ink or agave green (the blue is the one colour that doesn't come from the papel picado) and let marigold, which only reaches 1.96:1 on cream, act as the accent tying the picado to the chips.

Give the prices a little more presence for the lens: set them 12-13 pt (they are 11.5 pt now, only about 1 pt above the item names) or use a hairline dotted leader in the card colour, so the price column reads as a designed column rather than a stray numeral at the right edge.

Take the 'glass / bottle TBC' placeholder off the printed piece. A proof marker on a guest-facing menu is unpublishable, and its muted italic under the Brut Rosé price breaks the price style used on every other item.

The terracotta price on the featured card (#F3E3CB) measures only 5.08:1, the weakest price contrast. Darken terracotta to about #93330F, or lighten the featured face, to bring it above 6:1 so it matches the agave and blue cards.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country

measurements.header_level_sizes: card title Fraunces 700 12pt caps on every band; subheads DM Sans 700 7pt caps on every card
measurements.palette_count: 6 chromatic/ink colours (terracotta, agave, rosa, agave blue, marigold, ink) plus cream/muted, above the 2-4 target
measurements.content_check: 14 item_name, 14 description, 14 price; cocktails name spirit + 2 or more ingredients

top_problem: The lotería tabla is the stock Mexican-restaurant move (papel picado plus lotería cards) and it stops at the card faces. The drink lists underneath are generic cream lists on heavy outlined boxes. The boldest missing idea is running the lotería mechanic through the whole menu: each drink as its own numbered mini-card or tabla square, with the 'la carta' call-and-verse voice, a real venue name, and a printed game layer. That would make the menu ownable instead of themed.
fixes: Take the lotería system into the lists: give each drink its own lotería number and a small cut-paper glyph, or set each section as a 4-square tabla grid, so the concept carries the content and does not only decorate it.

Rebuild La Botella's face so the bottle is the same share of the face as the other cards (about 0.74, not 0.56) and the verse is centred on the figure. At the moment a tiny bottle floats in an empty band and breaks the one-composition system.

Cut the palette to terracotta, agave and rosa plus marigold as the accent. Drop agave blue, and thin the 3pt frames plus 0.75pt inset hairlines to one frame, so the tabla reads as printed cards and not as heavy UI boxes.

Replace the harsh black ink number chips with numerals printed straight onto the card face in the traditional lotería style (ink numeral, no box), and replace the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead with a designed wordmark that belongs to the venue.

Remove the 'glass / bottle TBC' proof marker from the printed page, and give the beer, wine and spirits lines a second typographic tier (style, ABV and region set small-caps in the card colour). That fills out the one-line lists so the right column and La Botella stop reading as sparse.

lens: phone version and print/phone coherence (preview-phone.png vs preview-letter.png)
top_problem: The phone keeps print's card order and styling, but it only restacks the printed tabla: four lotería cards in one tall column with a 2x2 grid of boxed tab buttons that looks like a form. Nothing uses the phone's own strengths. Paired with the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead and sparse beer and wine cards, the lotería idea reads as familiar Mexican-restaurant trim, not an ownable system. The boldest missing idea is to make the phone an actual lotería deal: a sticky one-row strip of the four numbered mini-cards (44 / 8 / 9 / 41) that the guest 'draws' from, each opening its card face, so print is the tabla and phone is the deck.
fixes: Replace the phone's 2x2 bordered tab buttons with a single sticky row of four small lotería card chips (number chip + figure icon, active card in its colour), so the navigation uses the card system and stops costing two rows of the viewport.

Print one serve-cue rule on both formats: the Daiquiri cue runs inline on the phone while the other three sit on their own line, and in print the Margarita and Manhattan cues run inline while the other two break. Always set the italic cue on its own line under the description.
Remove 'glass / bottle TBC' from the Brut Rosé on both print and phone: a published menu cannot show a placeholder, so either get the bottle price or print the glass price alone.

Give the thin beer and wine cards more visual weight on the phone, where each one-line 'Dry red wine.' entry sits under a card face as tall as El Cantarito's. Scale each phone face to its card's content, as print does (La Botella's face is 81 pt in print but full-height on the phone), or add style/ABV and grape/region lines once they are sourced.

Replace the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead with the venue's real name set as a lotería title card (framed, numbered), and reduce the phone papel picado from five cropped flags to a full-width string matching print's rhythm, so both formats open on the same ownable mark.

lens: Every item and price in round-11 doc.json, layout.json, proposal.md and preview-letter.png checked against build/draft_doc.json
top_problem: All 14 items and all 14 prices match the draft exactly (16/14/15/15, 12/16/18, 7/8/7/8, 12/11/13), and nothing is invented or dropped. But the copy is thin and some of it is unsourced. Half the list (spirits, beer, cider, wine) prints only the draft's placeholder words: 'Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.', 'Tequila blanco, by the pour.'. There are no ABVs, regions or ages. The missing facts are flagged, but the guest still gets a price list, not a menu. Serve cues that are not in the draft snapshot are printed as fact: 'orange peel', 'lime coin', 'In a coupe' (Daiquiri and Manhattan), 'On the rocks, lime wheel'. They cite an unnamed 'recipe' with no row ids. In doc.json, the designer also removed the draft's public_components hide on the Manhattan's aromatic-bitters on their own call, which is a change to the venue's data. Agave spirits are this cantina's signature, but they sit on the smallest, weakest card (La Botella: 45 pt figure, bottom-left), so the categories are not treated equally.
fixes: Restore Manhattan meta.public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false} as the draft has it, and put the conflict between that hide and menu_description on the needs_input list for the venue to decide; the designer does not settle it.

For every serve cue not in draft_doc.json (orange peel, lime coin, coupe x2, on the rocks, lime wheel), either cite the phg.recipe_versions id in the source table or print only what the draft has (serve_format and the Cocktail Cherry component), and flag the rest in missing_ingredients.

Give La Botella (the agave card) a face and figure scale equal to the other cards and consider moving it top-right, so a Mexican cantina's tequila list is not the least prominent category. Make the Z reading order (Cocktails, Beer, Spirits, Wine) a deliberate choice or change it.
Take the guest-facing 'glass / bottle TBC' off the printed Brut Rosé line and keep it only in the proof notes and needs_input, so the price reads as clean as the other 13.

Push the Coordinator to get ABV (beer and cider), region (wine) and age or brand (spirits) before the next round. Until then, stop the stock lines from simply restating the item's category ('Dry red wine.' under Malbec, 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' under Dry-Hopped IPA).

top_problem: Only the 4 cocktails meet the ingredient standard. The 10 spirits, beer, cider and wine lines are one-line stubs: no ABV, region, age or brand, and 'Tequila blanco, by the pour.' just repeats the item name. These gaps are honestly flagged in missing_ingredients, but half the menu still reads as a placeholder. The layout also puts Spirits second in column reading order and leaves the Margarita, the cantina's signature, below two whiskey and rum house drinks.
fixes: Get the missing facts from the venue through the Coordinator (beer and cider ABV and brewery, wine region and producer, tequila brand and añejo age, Cognac house), then rewrite each stub from those facts so no line only repeats its item name.

Until the facts arrive, rewrite the spirits lines so they stop echoing the name, using only draft facts (for example 'Unaged agave spirit, served neat' only if the draft supports it), and keep the missing_ingredients flags.
Reorder the panels so the reading order is Cocktails, Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits: put La Rosa under El Barril in reading sequence and La Botella last, which is the standard flow for this menu type.
Move Margarita to the first cocktail slot (or lead with Classics), because the best-selling agave cocktail belongs in the prime spot at a Mexican cantina.

Label the wine prices as glass or bottle (for example a small 'glass' cue on Malbec and Pinot Grigio, matching Brut Rosé's marker once it is confirmed) so price format is the same across the wine panel.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: For a cantina, the flow does not lead with agave. The prime spot on the featured card (the top of El Cantarito) goes to a Brown Butter Old Fashioned and a Daiquiri. The Margarita, the drink this venue is most likely to sell, sits third under 'Classics'. The agave spirits are on the smallest card, bottom-left, the weakest spot on the page, and share a subhead with Cognac. Wine's decorative face takes 51% of its card for three one-line items. The menu reads as a generic cocktail bar dressed in lotería art, not a Mexican cantina's drinks list.
fixes: Move the Margarita to the first slot on El Cantarito (or make it a 'De la Casa' lead with the agave drinks), and put the Old Fashioned and Daiquiri after it, so the prime spot sells the venue's signature.

Give agave the prime second position: move La Botella to the top-right card, split its subhead into 'Agave' (Blanco, Añejo) and 'Brandy' (Cognac VSOP), and move beer and wine down, so the reading order is cocktails, agave, beer, wine.
Shrink La Rosa's face from 51% of the card to about 36%, the same as the others, and give the space back to the list, so a three-item wine card no longer outweighs the cocktails visually.

Take the guest-facing 'glass / bottle TBC' proof marker off the Brut Rosé price, and label the pours in the section headers ('glass' for the wines, pour sizes for spirits and beer) once the venue answers, so prices are never unlabelled or show internal notes.

The beer, cider and wine lines are one-line placeholders ('Dry red wine.') next to the full cocktail specs, so the categories are not treated equally: press the Coordinator for the needs_input answers (ABV and style for beer and cider; region, grape and producer for wine; and whether a non-alcoholic section exists, which is expected in a college town) before the next round rather than printing the gaps.

top_problem: The menu reads in two voices. The four cocktails get full copy: ingredients, a character lead and an italic serve cue. The other ten items get bare three-word category tags ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.', 'Dry sparkling cider.'), and the spirits just repeat their own names back ('Blanco Tequila' / 'Tequila blanco, by the pour.'). Against the bold lotería concept, half the list feels like an unfinished database export. On top of that, 'DRAFT & CIDER' says every beer is on draft, but the draft only calls the IPA draft and marks the cider's format as unknown.
fixes: Rename the 'DRAFT & CIDER' subhead to 'Beer & Cider' (or just 'Cerveza & Sidra') until the venue confirms which pours are on draft, because right now the header states a serve fact the draft does not support.

Rewrite the three spirit lines so they add something instead of repeating the name (e.g. 'Unaged agave spirit, poured neat.' only if the venue confirms the serve; if not, leave the description empty and mark it missing_ingredients), and push brand, age and pour size to the venue as the first needs_input question.

Treat every item the same way. Either give the House Originals a character lead drawn from draft facts, as Margarita and Manhattan have, or drop the leads from the two classics, so the featured card does not describe its signature drinks in less voice than its standards.

Take the proof-stage 'glass / bottle TBC' note off the guest-facing layout (keep it in the needs_input flag), and once pour data arrives, label every beer and wine price with one consistent pour label in the price column.

Resolve the verse-tone flag before approval: swap the two drunkenness verses on La Botella and El Barril for other traditional cantor lines, or have the venue sign them off. Also make the headers consistently Spanish or consistently English (for example 'Cocteles' under El Cantarito), so the language on the cards matches the concept.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged (vs build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: Items and prices are right: all 14 match the draft and nothing was invented or dropped (Dry Cider moved from sec_cider into Beer with its id and price kept). Most of the missing data is flagged correctly in meta.missing_ingredients and needs_input. But 10 of the 14 items print without the facts their category needs: beer has no style/ABV, wine no region/producer, spirits no brand/age, and there are no pour sizes. A proof marker, 'glass / bottle TBC', is printed on the guest-facing Brut Rosé line. And the cocktail garnishes and glassware (orange peel, coupe, lime coin, lime wheel, Manhattan coupe) are not in the draft; they are credited to 'recipe' but no recipe_versions row id is given.
fixes: Take the 'glass / bottle TBC' proof marker off the printed and phone menu. Keep the question only in meta.missing_ingredients / needs_input, and hold publication (needs_input=true) until the venue answers glass or bottle so the $13 gets a proper label.

For every garnish and glass cue that is not in the draft (Old Fashioned orange peel and large cube; Daiquiri coupe and lime coin; Margarita lime wheel; Manhattan coupe), cite the phg.recipe_versions id and its garnish/glassware value in the source table, or drop the cue and flag it in missing_ingredients.

Add a guest-visible placeholder system in the proof version only, such as a consistent 'ABV / region to come' slot in the description measure, so the layout already reserves space for the beer style/ABV, wine region and spirit brand/age lines and does not reflow when the venue supplies them.
Put the dairy allergen flag for the Brown Butter Old Fashioned first in the needs_input list, and prepare the printed allergen marker style now so it can go live the moment the venue confirms.

Set and state one reading order for the 2 + 2 tabla (Cocktails, Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits, or Cocktails, Spirits, Beer, Wine) and match the phone tab order to it, so both formats present every drinks category in the same logical sequence.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass and serve to sources; Mexican restaurant + cocktail bar, Iowa City
top_problem: The facts are accurate but the writing is thin: 3 spirits and 3 wines print descriptions that only repeat the item name or a category ('Tequila blanco, by the pour.', 'VSOP Cognac, by the pour.', 'Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.'). A guest-proof 'glass / bottle TBC' marker is printed on the Brut Rosé line, and no wine price says whether it is a glass or a bottle.
sources: phg.menu_items + phg.recipe_versions (project ddc4bb5b, designer_query log_id 165): Brown Butter Old Fashioned, garnish 'Orange peel', method 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube', desc 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara, bitters.' Printed text matches.
House Daiquiri: glass Coupe, garnish 'Lime coin', desc 'White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup.' Matches; 'fresh' is added.

Margarita: glass Rocks, garnish 'Lime wheel', method '...strain over fresh ice', desc 'Tequila blanco, lime, orange liqueur, agave. Bright and citrus-forward.' Matches; 'fresh lime' and 'agave syrup' go beyond the source ('lime', 'agave').
Manhattan: glass Coupe, garnish 'Cocktail cherry', desc 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.' Matches; 'rye whiskey' is a fair expansion.

Beer, cider, wine and spirits: no recipe version exists. The printed lines trace word for word to menu_items.menu_description (Crisp pale lager / Hop-forward draft IPA / Toasty amber lager / Dry sparkling cider / Dry red wine / Dry white wine / Dry sparkling rosé / 'Blanco tequila pour' / 'Añejo tequila pour' / 'VSOP Cognac pour'). Accents on Añejo and Rosé are correct.
The draft menu_items include 'Junmai Ginjo' (12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.'), and it is not on the menu. This is the content reviewer's call, but it affects coherence.

The lotería verses and Don Clemente numbers (8 La Botella, 9 El Barril, 41 La Rosa, 44 El Cantarito) match the traditional deck. Not checked against the database; this is cultural reference, not item fact.

Not checked: recipe_components came back empty (ingredients null) for all 4 cocktails, so every ingredient was traced through menu_description only. Per the protocol, an empty lookup is not evidence that a fact is unsourced.
fixes: Rewrite the spirit and wine lines in guest language using only draft facts plus spirit_lexicon or beverage_categories rows (for example, what añejo ageing means), so no description just repeats its name; where there is no source, flag missing_ingredients (grape region, producer, beer ABV) and ask instead of printing a category word.

Remove the printed 'glass / bottle TBC' proof marker from the guest menu and move the question to proposal needs_input; once the draft gives a label, print one consistent 'glass' or 'glass / bottle' label for all three wines.
Change 'fresh lime' to 'lime' and 'agave syrup' to 'agave' in the Margarita and Daiquiri lines unless a recipe_components or prep_recipes row confirms them, so every printed word traces exactly.
Use the venue's real name in the title if phg.menu_projects or accounts has it; 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' reads as a placeholder and weakens the otherwise strong lotería and Spanish-verse venue fit.
Put the Margarita and Manhattan serve cues on their own italic line, the way the Old Fashioned and Daiquiri cues are set, so all four cocktails read the same in print.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: The menu speaks in two voices. The four cocktails get real guest lines with italic serve cues. The other 10 items print their category or just repeat their own name: 'Tequila blanco, by the pour.' (Blanco Tequila), 'Tequila añejo, by the pour.', 'VSOP Cognac, by the pour.', 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', 'Toasty amber lager.', 'Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.'. That breaks the criterion-12 rule against repeating the item name or using taxonomy wording. Every printed fact does trace to a source: phg.menu_items.menu_description plus phg.recipe_versions via current_recipe_version_id (gateway log_id 161). Old Fashioned: Rocks, 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube', Orange peel. Daiquiri: Coupe, Lime coin. Margarita: Rocks, 'strain over fresh ice', Lime wheel, 'Bright and citrus-forward'. Manhattan: Coupe, Cocktail cherry, 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.'. So the fix is to get more words from the venue, not to invent them. The design is also missing the categories a Mexican cantina guest expects (mezcal, a Mexican lager, a Paloma or other agave drinks, non-alcoholic / agua fresca), and nothing in the proposal asks the venue for them.
fixes: Put a needs_input request in proposal.md for one sourced character phrase per spirit, beer and wine: tequila brand and age, cognac house, brewery, style and ABV, wine producer and region. Until those arrive, drop the name-echo lines, for example print the beverage_categories wording ('Blanco / plata') or a single measure like '1.5 oz pour' if the venue confirms it, rather than 'Tequila blanco, by the pour.'

Give all four cocktails the same pattern: a character lead only where the draft has one, the same ingredient wording ('demerara' in the Old Fashioned but 'house demerara syrup' in the Daiquiri; use one), and the serve cue placed the same way every time. Right now it sits on its own line for the Old Fashioned and Daiquiri but runs inline for the Margarita and Manhattan. 'Over one large cube' should read 'over a large cube', matching the recipe_versions method text.
Take the internal 'glass / bottle TBC' proof marker off the guest-facing Brut Rosé line. Keep it in proposal.md, and label the wine prices glass or bottle once the venue confirms the pour.

Venue fit: ask the Coordinator and the venue for the agave-forward and Mexican items a guest at an Iowa City cantina will look for: mezcal, a Mexican lager, a Paloma, a non-alcoholic agua fresca. As printed, the lists (Czech Pilsner, Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Manhattan) could belong to any bar. The lotería verses are authentic Don Clemente copy and spelled correctly (cántaro, bebió, albañil), so keep them. Also note that menu_items includes 'Junmai Ginjo' (sake), which is left off the menu without any note.

Wording only: 'Spirit-forward' comes from the draft meta.family class ('Spirit-Forward'). Write it as guest language, or drop it so the Manhattan matches the Daiquiri, which has no lead because the draft gives it no character words.

lens: venue-type fit: Mexican cantina and cocktail bar, Spanish and lotería usage including verses, census ZIP 52240
top_problem: The lotería layer is only decoration on top of a generic American bar list, and it isn't accurate. The La Rosa verse is misquoted: the menu prints 'ven que te quiero ver', but the traditional Don Clemente cantor verse is 'Rosita, Rosaura, ven que te quiero ahora'. Behind the cards, the drinks are not a cantina's. There is one agave cocktail out of four, no mezcal, a Czech Pilsner and an Amber Lager but no Mexican beer, and Cognac filed under 'Agave & Brandy'. Seven of the 14 descriptions only repeat the item name or its category ('Dry red wine.', 'Tequila blanco, by the pour.'). Verified: all four card numbers are correct (8 La Botella, 9 El Barril, 41 La Rosa, 44 El Cantarito), and the Cantarito, Barril and Botella verses are the traditional texts. Every cocktail glass, garnish and serve cue matches phg.recipe_versions through menu_items.current_recipe_version_id (gateway log_id 166): Old Fashioned Rocks / Orange peel / 'strain over a large cube'; Daiquiri Coupe / Lime coin; Margarita Rocks / Lime wheel / 'strain over fresh ice'; Manhattan Coupe / Cocktail cherry. The lead-ins 'Bright and citrus-forward' and 'aromatic bitters' are in menu_items.menu_description. Census ZCTA 52240 (acs2024_5yr, log_id 166): median age 28.6, median household income $52,960, Hispanic/Latino 3,868 of 35,074 (11.0%). This is a student market where $15-16 cocktails are the top of the local price tier, so the menu needs a value anchor it doesn't have.
problems: Unsourced or misquoted cultural text: the printed La Rosa verse 'Rosita, Rosaura, ven que te quiero ver.' differs from the traditional lotería verse 'Rosita, Rosaura, ven que te quiero ahora.'

Unsourced claim: the subhead 'DRAFT & CIDER' says the beers are on draft, but only Dry-Hopped IPA has 'draft' in its menu_description ('Hop-forward draft IPA.'). Czech Pilsner, Amber Lager and Dry Cider have no serve format in the data, and proposal.md itself lists the cider's format as missing.

Descriptions that only repeat the name or category (criterion 12): 'Tequila blanco, by the pour.' / 'Tequila añejo, by the pour.' / 'VSOP Cognac, by the pour.' repeat the item names with the words flipped, and 'Dry red wine.' / 'Dry white wine.' / 'Dry sparkling rosé.' / 'Dry sparkling cider.' are class labels. Half the menu reads like a database. The two voices clash: the cocktails are written in rich guest language, the rest in bare labels.

Venue fit: only the Margarita is agave-based. Three of four cocktails (Old Fashioned, Daiquiri, Manhattan) and the beer list (Czech Pilsner, Amber Lager, IPA) could belong to any Iowa City bar. Cognac in 'AGAVE & BRANDY' dilutes the agave card. There is no mezcal, no Mexican lager and no non-alcoholic agua fresca, all of which a cantina guest expects. Reference 572 (Coa Cantina Iowa City) leads with agave, and this menu does not.

Language mix: the card names are Spanish, but every subhead is English ('HOUSE ORIGINALS', 'CLASSICS', 'RED, WHITE & SPARKLING'). The Spanish 'Tequila blanco' / 'Tequila añejo' descriptions sit under English item names ('Blanco Tequila', 'Añejo Tequila'), so one item uses two word orders.

Responsible-service tone: 'La herramienta del borracho.' and 'Tanto bebió el albañil, que quedó como barril.' are authentic, but they sit directly over the spirits and beer lists. In a college town (median age 28.6) that reads as encouraging heavy drinking. proposal.md flags 7 correctly leaves this to the venue.

Layout (criterion 14): 'glass / bottle TBC' is a proof note printed on the guest menu. The wine prices have no glass or pour label at all, and the spirits have no pour size, so the prices float without a unit. The La Botella face spends 81 pt on a single verse line while its three items get two-word descriptions.
fixes: Correct the La Rosa verse to the traditional 'Rosita, Rosaura, ven que te quiero ahora.' (or cite a documented variant), and check all four verses against one named lotería source.

Change the 'DRAFT & CIDER' subhead to something that makes no serve claim (for example 'Cerveza & Sidra'), or get the draft/can format for each beer and the cider from the venue before printing 'draft'.

Bring the subheads into the same Spanish-first voice as the card names, with English support ('De la Casa / House Originals', 'Clásicos', 'Agave', 'Tintos, Blancos y Espumosos'), and make the tequila descriptions match their English item names.

Send the venue a needs_input request for cantina-core items: a Mexican lager, a mezcal pour, a second agave cocktail and an agua fresca or other non-alcoholic option. Move Cognac off the agave card or rename the subhead. Do not invent any of these.

Replace the category-only lines with data-backed guest copy once brand, region and ABV arrive. Until then, drop the repeated '… by the pour' and label glass or bottle and pour size in the price column, not as a 'TBC' proof note.
